report.headline: Sound-led opening, strong visual peak in the middle; understanding lands the joke late
report.summary: The ad runs well above typical viewing through its midsection, with seeing as the dominant group and hearing carrying the first few seconds before visuals take over. Understanding rises in the final third as the comedy payoff and brand message land. The boardroom sequence is the weakest stretch before the close, where hearing dips below typical and overall falls to its lowest point in the main body of the ad.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera speaks directly to camera, holding nothing yet, with dramatic lighting and music.
moments.brain_response: Hearing is well above typical from the first frame and carries engagement while seeing builds gradually — a sound-led opening that works.

moments.what_happens: He turns back to camera holding the CeraVe jar with a knowing smile, saying 'you didn't know?'
moments.brain_response: Seeing joins hearing well above typical, producing the first clear combined peak and the strongest hearing moment of the video.

moments.what_happens: Two faces appear in the spa headrest comedy shot, followed by a climber scaling a rock face in a sweeping landscape.
moments.brain_response: Seeing reaches its highest level of the entire video, sustaining the peak across both scenes; overall is at its strongest here.
moments.suggestion: These are your two best visual moments — the abrupt cut between them works; consider whether the climber shot could be slightly longer to hold the peak.

moments.what_happens: The boardroom scene continues with the presentation footage playing on the screen behind the presenter.
moments.brain_response: Hearing falls below typical for the first time, dragging overall to its lowest point in the main body of the ad.
moments.suggestion: A stronger music cue or a sound design beat here could support the comedic reveal and lift the weakest stretch.

moments.what_happens: The camera cuts to a close-up of three dermatologists in front of the CeraVe logo, then to Michael Cera smiling and gesturing.
moments.brain_response: Understanding rises to its highest level of the video as the name-connection joke and brand credentials land together.

moments.what_happens: A product card reads 'Developed with Dermatologists. Not Michael Cera.' alongside the CeraVe jar.
moments.brain_response: Seeing falls below typical and overall drops below 0 by the final seconds — a normal close for a product card of this length.

strengths: Hearing builds engagement from the very first frame, giving the ad a confident start before the visuals are fully established.
The spa comedy shot and the rock-climbing sequence form a sustained visual peak that is the strongest engagement stretch in the ad.
improvements: Hearing fades across the second half and drops below typical through the boardroom sequence — a more distinctive audio layer there would support the comedy payoff at the moment it most needs it.

Seeing declines steadily from the three-person shot at around 16 seconds onward, so the brand message arrives on a falling visual curve; a brief return to a face alongside the product card could maintain engagement through the close.

report.headline: A well-above-typical ad led by hearing and understanding: the comedy dialogue is where it peaks
report.summary: The video runs well above typical for most of its length, with hearing the dominant driver whenever Michael Cera speaks directly to camera and understanding rising during the comedy lines. Seeing holds above typical through the long middle section. A below-typical opening and two quieter stretches with little speech are the clearest opportunities.

moments.what_happens: The video opens on dark curtains parting to reveal a silhouetted figure, with no face or product on screen.
moments.brain_response: All three groups sit below typical, making this the only stretch before the main content where overall engagement is clearly below zero.
moments.suggestion: Showing the product or a face even a second or two earlier would bring this opening up to at least typical from the start.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera faces the camera, introduces himself by name, and holds up the CeraVe cream.
moments.brain_response: Hearing jumps to the highest point in the entire video as music and speech combine; overall rises sharply to well above typical.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera peers through a sheer curtain with 'GENEROSITY' on screen, then steps forward and declares 'I am CeraVe.'
moments.brain_response: The video's highest and most sustained overall peak, with hearing and understanding both clearly above typical at the same time.

moments.what_happens: A wordless wide-angle rock-climbing sequence plays with no dialogue and no close-up of Michael Cera.
moments.brain_response: Hearing drops to its lowest level in the video, falling below typical; overall weakens to just above typical, the weakest stretch in the middle section.
moments.suggestion: A short line of voiceover from Michael Cera here would keep hearing above typical through this action sequence.

moments.what_happens: A CGI narwhal in a fantasy lagoon exchanges compliments with Michael Cera, with the dialogue carried only by on-screen subtitles.
moments.brain_response: Hearing and understanding both fall below typical as audible sound design recedes; seeing alone keeps overall barely above typical.
moments.suggestion: Having Michael Cera speak his reply aloud rather than relying solely on subtitles would bring hearing and understanding back above typical here.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera stands alone in close-up, gazing quietly at the CeraVe cream.
moments.brain_response: Seeing and hearing both slip below typical and overall briefly falls below zero, the lowest point in the main content.
moments.suggestion: Cutting to the wider three-person group shot a second or two sooner could prevent this brief dip below typical.

strengths: The video sustains above-typical overall engagement across most of its length, with hearing well above typical in every stretch where Michael Cera speaks directly to camera.
The visual variety across settings—curtained studio, spa, rock face, fantasy lagoon—keeps seeing above typical throughout the long middle section even when hearing dips.
improvements: The video's strongest engagement is concentrated in the first third; placing a larger comedy beat or surprising visual reveal after the 50-second mark would rebuild the peak that gradually fades in the second half.

With the sound off, the response stays close to typical throughout, meaning the pictures alone do not distinguish the ad strongly—more visually unexpected shots could strengthen engagement for viewers who cannot hear it.

report.headline: Sintel trailer peaks strongly in its middle with voice and face, but dark bookends hold back overall engagement
report.summary: The trailer opens below typical on dark frames but builds from second 10 as hearing and character faces drive a well-above-typical peak. Sound lifts overall clearly above pictures-only through this stretch. Seeing peaks at the creature attack while hearing drops away, blunting the climax. A long logo and credits tail closes well below typical.

moments.what_happens: The trailer opens on a black screen that fades into a barely visible dark snowy landscape.
moments.brain_response: Overall sits below typical throughout, with understanding well below 0 and seeing near 0, leaving no group above typical.
moments.suggestion: Opening immediately on the warrior character in the snowstorm rather than the black fade-in would bring engagement above typical sooner.

moments.what_happens: A production title card gives way to a tight close-up of the elder character asking about the land of the gatekeepers.
moments.brain_response: Hearing reaches the highest point in the entire trailer, well above typical, and lifts overall well above what the pictures alone would deliver.

moments.what_happens: A snow fight gives way to the protagonist running through a ruined city, then an epic golden-hour aerial shot of crumbling towers with creatures in flight.
moments.brain_response: Seeing climbs steadily while hearing remains well above typical, sustaining the trailer's highest and most consistent overall engagement.

moments.what_happens: A creature swoops at the protagonist in open sky and a close-up of its snapping jaws fills the frame.
moments.brain_response: Seeing reaches its peak for the whole video, but hearing falls below typical, pulling overall down sharply from the sustained high of the previous stretch.
moments.suggestion: A strong music hit or sound design accent at the moment of attack would align the audio and visual peaks and maintain overall engagement.

moments.what_happens: A lone figure crosses vast empty desert dunes as the title Sintel fades onto the frame.
moments.brain_response: This is the weakest stretch in the main content, with seeing below typical; hearing rises with the music but only holds overall near typical.
moments.suggestion: A brief cut to a character face before the title appears would lift seeing and give the title reveal a stronger emotional base.

moments.what_happens: The Sintel logo holds on a black screen for several seconds, followed by a full credits card.
moments.brain_response: Overall falls well below typical and continues falling to the last second, driven by seeing going strongly negative on the near-empty frames.
moments.suggestion: Trimming the logo and credits to around five seconds total would prevent the prolonged slide below typical.

strengths: The sustained run of close-up character faces from seconds 12 through 27 keeps seeing well above typical for an extended stretch, giving the trailer strong visual anchoring.
Sound and speech work together from seconds 10 through 28, keeping overall consistently and measurably higher than the pictures-only level throughout the trailer's core.
improvements: The two dark black-screen passages in the first twelve seconds rely entirely on audio; a visual backdrop behind the production title card would avoid dipping below typical before the story even begins.

Seeing and hearing reach their individual highs at different points in the trailer; timing a strong music swell to coincide with the creature-attack visual peak around seconds 28 to 30 could produce a single unified climax.

report.headline: Charming animated short with strong visual peaks — a quiet middle stretch is the main opportunity
report.summary: This short runs above typical for much of its runtime, with seeing leading throughout and hearing joining strongly in the finale. The opening sits just below typical for the first seven seconds before climbing as the bunny's face fills the frame. A quiet apple-holding passage around seconds 29 to 39 pulls overall to the video's lowest point and is the clearest opportunity to improve.

moments.what_happens: The bunny sprints from its burrow and the camera tilts up to show it looking contentedly at the sky.
moments.brain_response: Overall stays just below typical throughout, with hearing and understanding both below 0 while seeing is only slightly above.
moments.suggestion: Moving to a close-up of the bunny's expressive face a few seconds sooner, or adding a stronger musical hook from the first frame, could push overall above typical earlier.

moments.what_happens: The bunny presses its face deep into the daisies, then a large butterfly lands on it as it lies in the grass.
moments.brain_response: Overall climbs to one of the two highest points of the video, with seeing well above typical and hearing also clearly above typical.

moments.what_happens: The bunny stands alone in the open meadow, quietly examining the apple it has picked up, with little movement.
moments.brain_response: Overall sinks to the lowest point of the video and stays below typical, driven by hearing falling well below typical while seeing drops near and below 0.
moments.suggestion: More dynamic musical energy during this reflective pause, or cutting to a closer reaction shot of the bunny's face sooner, could recover engagement.

moments.what_happens: A butterfly lands on the bunny's head and then its nose; the bunny reacts with wide-eyed surprise and says thank you.
moments.brain_response: Overall matches the first peak and is clearly above typical, with hearing reaching the highest point in the video and understanding also rising well above typical, both lifting overall noticeably above what the pictures alone would achieve.

strengths: Close-up shots of the bunny's expressive face drive seeing well above typical across multiple stretches, forming the visual backbone of the film.
The final sequence brings all three groups above typical at once, giving the short a strong and engaged close.
improvements: The middle stretch around seconds 29 to 39 is the weakest part of the video; the hearing response falls well below typical during the quiet apple-holding pause, suggesting a more dynamic score or shorter pause would help.
The opening sits just below typical for its first seven seconds; cutting to a tight face shot of the bunny sooner could push overall above typical from the start.

report.headline: Video B peaks higher in its active middle but A holds up far better at both ends
report.summary: These are two different Blender Foundation animations — the cheerful rabbit short (A) and the fantasy adventure Sintel (B). B draws stronger peak engagement through its active middle, lifted by powerful sound design and spoken dialogue, but its long title-card ending drags the response deeply below typical viewing. A is more consistent throughout and never falls far below typical.

differences.what_differs: A opens on a bright, colourful rabbit emerging from a mossy burrow, keeping seeing above typical from the first second; B opens on a completely black screen fading to dark, featureless snowscapes, holding all groups well below typical for the first several seconds.
differences.brain_response: A's seeing starts positive and hearing stays close to typical, giving A a clear early advantage, while B's opening is below typical across all groups.

differences.what_differs: B cuts to close-up dialogue between a weathered elder and the red-haired protagonist, accompanied by a strong musical score; A continues with the rabbit sniffing flowers in a sunny meadow with no speech.
differences.brain_response: B's hearing response spikes far above typical during this stretch and understanding climbs clearly positive as well, driving B's overall well above A's; A's understanding stays below typical throughout and hearing remains low, so A falls noticeably behind.

differences.what_differs: A continues with the rabbit's comedic encounters — butterflies landing on its head, expressions of surprise — keeping the character on screen; B transitions to a title card ('SINTEL') on a black background that holds for roughly ten seconds, then cuts to a credits screen.
differences.brain_response: A's seeing, hearing, and overall all rise and stay clearly above typical through to the end; B's seeing falls sharply below typical and stays deeply negative, pulling B's overall well below typical for the final stretch.

a_does_better: A's opening is above typical from the first second because the main character is visible and the scene is bright, giving it an immediate advantage over B's dark, empty start.
A maintains a consistently positive response through its final ten seconds, while B's long title card causes a sustained drop far below typical viewing.
b_does_better: B's sound design and orchestral score drive hearing to exceptionally high levels through the middle of the video — well above anything A achieves — and this carries B's overall to its strongest peaks.
B's action sequences from the ruined city to the desert, combined with spoken dialogue, lift understanding clearly above typical, a group that stays flat or below typical in A throughout.
suggestions: Trim B's title card to no more than three or four seconds, or replace the final black screens with a held frame from the desert scene, to prevent the steep fall that currently ends the video well below typical.

A could benefit from a richer music track or sound design that builds through the middle section, as the sound contributes little lift compared to the pictures; closing that gap would raise A's overall closer to B's peaks.

report.headline: Video B sustains stronger engagement across most of its runtime; Video A's immediate opening is its clearest advantage
report.summary: These are two cuts of the same CeraVe campaign featuring Michael Cera. B, the extended cut, runs above typical overall from about second 10 onward and reaches higher peaks, carried mainly by hearing and understanding in its middle third. A opens stronger — above typical from the first second — but ends well below typical while B stays comfortably above it through nearly all of its remaining runtime.

differences.what_differs: A opens immediately with Michael Cera speaking to camera, so seeing and hearing are both above typical from the first second. B opens on dark, empty curtains with no speech, and all three groups stay below typical until his face appears around second 7.
differences.brain_response: A's overall is clearly above typical throughout this stretch; B's overall stays clearly below typical for the same period, a meaningful early gap that costs B engagement it never fully recovers against A's opening.

differences.what_differs: By the time A reaches the boardroom scene with dermatologists reviewing footage, its overall is declining toward typical. In B's equivalent stretch, Michael Cera is speaking directly to camera holding the product, and hearing and understanding are both well above typical.
differences.brain_response: B's overall in this stretch is roughly double A's, driven by hearing and understanding while seeing stays at a similar level in both; this is where B clearly pulls ahead.

differences.what_differs: B contains a unique narwhal and fantasy-forest sequence absent from A, where a CGI narwhal speaks on screen. Seeing stays above typical, but hearing and understanding fall to near or below typical.
differences.brain_response: Overall in B dips to its lowest point since the opening during this stretch, with sound and speech no longer contributing; the pictures carry it alone, making this the weakest section in an otherwise well-sustained video.

a_does_better: A opens with above-typical engagement across seeing and hearing from the very first second, giving it an immediate head-start that B's dark-curtain opening cannot match.
b_does_better: B sustains above-typical overall engagement from roughly second 10 through second 72, including several scenes with no equivalent in A, where hearing and understanding together lift engagement well above typical.

B's peak overall level, reached during the mid-section speech-to-camera passages, is higher than A's peak, showing the extended material adds genuine engagement when Michael Cera is on screen with the product.
suggestions: Replace or shorten B's dark, silent curtain opening — cutting to Michael Cera's face by second 2 or 3 would bring hearing and understanding above typical from the start, as A already does.
Add voiceover or music to B's narwhal and fantasy-forest sequence (roughly B 46–52) to lift hearing and understanding back toward typical and close the dip in overall engagement during that stretch.
